hits.author: ndriscoll
hits.comment_text: No streaming app is giving you a video feed with 48Gbps of data (more like 5-15 Mbps), and no one produces 120 or 144Hz video (most movies/TV are still 24Hz aren't they?), so there's no point in sending that kind of signal to a TV (you'll just have a crisp, high refresh signal of the low refresh blurry compression artifacts), but even ignoring that, cheap n100 minipcs can do 4k60 or 1k240 just fine (I use a minipc as my desktop with a 4k240 OLED).

hits.author: qlte
hits.comment_text:
> This is entirely too much effort

It really isn't. I've done this on like 4 different Android TV devices and it's like 30 minutes of effort at most and you only need to do it once.

If the alternative was a totally open Linux box you'd almost certainly spend way more time than that tweaking config and stuff (even if you'd mentally categorize than as "voluntary" time for a hobby and therefore not actually wasted).

I'll happily take that insignificant one time setup for a 100% ad-free experience (including Youtube) with a customizable launcher I can adjust to my liking on a 4K Android TV stick that cost me $39.99. And automate basically any function via ADB, including remapping the branded Netflix/HBO/etc buttons on the remote (I have a "Free TV" button that now goes to .... Stremio which I still laugh at occasionally).

I couldn't do any of that on a $199.99 Apple TV. An N100 Mini PC would cost 6x as much as I spent on an Onn stick, plus I'd need to buy a remote and would have to work around a keyboard/mouse centric UI and couldn't navigate with HDMI-CEC either.

I can't even think of anything I'm unable to do with my Custom Launcher/Sideload/Remote ADB Android TV setup like OP. It's just about the perfect couch-based interface. It does what I tell it without distractions and fades into the background completely like any good UI should, so I can focus on what I'm actually watching instead.

hits.author: stego-tech
hits.comment_text:
Shoutout to another happy N100 miniPC user! I have two myself from before the RAMpocalypse, with one doing standard Proxmox + VMs work in a similar vein to ESXi, and the other straight Debian + Docker for more container hands-on time. Just the perfect little homelab boxes at the perfect price point (~$180US) before things got insane.

My stack is currently a mix of usual end user services (Jellyfin, FreshRSS) and identity infra, and it chugs along brilliantly without issue. I’m fairly certain that I could leave it running to the heat death of the universe if I built lifecycle management into my backup scripts.

hits.author: Chu4eeno
hits.comment_text:
> NixOS has a longstanding issue where library loading (and therefore program start, particularly GUI programs that load a lot) is n^2, but programs still all start in ~1 second or less on my n100 minipc. I still found that to be annoying enough to look into why it seemed so slow (and learned about the loading issue). Can't imagine things taking so long that you actually switch to another task. The same minipc can easily handle my 4k 240hz HDR monitor as well, and the whole experience is completely smooth.

KDE actually solved that long time ago with kdeinit (https://web.archive.org/web/20010517071320/www.suse.de/~bast... and follow-up work by Lubos, see e. g. https://conference2005.kde.org/slides/kde-performance/index....), but the new crop of developers didn't notice much difference on their high-end systems with SSDs, so they ripped it out.
hits.story_title: If coding has been solved, why does software keep getting worse?

hits.author: ndriscoll
hits.comment_text:
Yeah the obvious answer to software getting worse is to switch to FOSS. Use Linux/KDE. It's been great for a long time and only ever gets better. It's as if Windows 7 just continued to slowly iterate and add useful polish.

NixOS has a longstanding issue where library loading (and therefore program start, particularly GUI programs that load a lot) is n^2, but programs still all start in ~1 second or less on my n100 minipc. I still found that to be annoying enough to look into why it seemed so slow (and learned about the loading issue). Can't imagine things taking so long that you actually switch to another task. The same minipc can easily handle my 4k 240hz HDR monitor as well, and the whole experience is completely smooth.

The computer also just obeys me. It does exactly what I tell it to, and nothing more.
